introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer 4 questions out of 5. Section B: answer 2 questions out of 3. Section C: answer both questions. Show all steps in calculations. Calculators are allowed.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown:
This question concerns the first four elements in Group I of the periodic table.

| Element | Lithium (Li) | Sodium (Na) | Potassium (K) | Rubidium (Rb) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Atomic number | 3 | 11 | 19 | 37 |
incertitudes: Le sujet se contredit : l'en-tête demande 4 questions sur 5 en Section A, mais le titre de la section dit « Answer ALL questions in this section ». La règle de l'en-tête est retenue.
Points imprimés 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12, pour « Total = 10 marks » : recopiés tels quels.
Pilote : seule la question 1 de la Section A est transcrite.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Why are they classified as Group I elements?

(ii) Which element is the least reactive?

(iii) Write the electronic configuration of potassium (K). *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Each has **one electron in its outer shell**, so they sit in the same group.

(ii) **Lithium** - reactivity increases down the group as the outer electron is lost more easily.

(iii) Potassium has 19 electrons: **2, 8, 8, 1**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) These elements are usually stored under paraffin. Explain.

(ii) Write an equation for the reaction between sodium and water. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) They are very reactive and react quickly with oxygen and moisture in the air; paraffin keeps air and water away.

(ii) $2\mathrm{Na} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{H_2}$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Lithium, though in Group I, resembles magnesium in Group II in its chemical properties.

(i) What name is given to this resemblance?

(ii) State the products formed when the carbonates of Li and Na are strongly heated: $\mathrm{Li_2CO_3}$ and $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **diagonal relationship**.

(ii) $\mathrm{Li_2CO_3}$ decomposes: $\mathrm{Li_2CO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{Li_2O} + \mathrm{CO_2}$. $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ does **not** decompose at Bunsen temperatures: no products.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the type of compound formed when Group I elements combine with non-metals. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Ionic compounds**: the metal atom loses its outer electron to form a positive ion, which bonds electrostatically with the negative ion of the non-metal.
